summary:
Manacher's algorithm. Insert `#` between letters (and sentinels at the ends) so every palindrome has odd length.
For each centre, start its radius from the mirror image inside the rightmost palindrome found so far, then
expand. Each radius `r` accounts for `(r + 1) / 2` palindromic substrings of `s`. O(n), with a 64-bit total.

question.md:
Count every palindromic substring of `s` (single letters included; equal substrings at different positions
count separately).

- **n up to 2 × 10⁵**: centre expansion is O(n²) on inputs like `aaaa…a`, too slow.
- **The count can reach ~2 × 10¹⁰**, beyond 32 bits.

think.md:
`"aabaa"` has **9** palindromic substrings.

Expanding from every centre is quadratic on repetitive strings because neighbouring centres redo the same
comparisons. Manacher's trick: inside a big palindrome centred at `C`, the picture is mirrored, so the radius at
position `i` is at least the radius at its mirror `2C − i` (capped at the big palindrome's edge). Only the part
beyond the right edge needs new comparisons, and that edge only moves right: O(n) total.

The `#` separators make even and odd palindromes look the same: every palindrome in the new string has a
centre on a character.

idea.md: For each of the 2n − 1 centres, expand while the ends match and count each step.

lines.text: Each matching step outward is one palindrome.

complexity.md: **Time O(n²)** worst case: 2 × 10¹⁰ steps on 2 × 10⁵ equal letters. **Space O(1).**

steps.text: Centre on letter 0 ('a'): expands 1 step(s) to 'a', then stops at the edge of the string. +1 palindromes.
Centre on the gap between 0 and 1: expands 1 step(s) to 'aa', then stops at the edge of the string. +1 palindromes.
Centre on letter 1 ('a'): expands 1 step(s) to 'a', then stops at 'a' ≠ 'b'. +1 palindromes.
Centre on letter 2 ('b'): expands 3 step(s) to 'aabaa', then stops at the edge of the string. +3 palindromes.
Centre on letter 3 ('a'): expands 1 step(s) to 'a', then stops at 'b' ≠ 'a'. +1 palindromes.
Centre on the gap between 3 and 4: expands 1 step(s) to 'aa', then stops at the edge of the string. +1 palindromes.
Centre on letter 4 ('a'): expands 1 step(s) to 'a', then stops at the edge of the string. +1 palindromes.

walk.title: Expand around each centre and count every successful step (O(n²) in the worst case).

limits.md: Neighbouring centres inside a long palindrome repeat the same comparisons. Manacher reuses the mirrored radius so every comparison moves the right edge forward.

idea.md: Build `t = ^#a#b#…#$`. Keep the palindrome reaching furthest right (`center`, `right`). For each `i`: start `p[i]` at `min(right − i, p[2·center − i])` if `i < right`, expand while the neighbours match, and update `center/right`. The answer is `Σ (p[i] + 1) / 2`.

lines.text: `#` between letters makes every palindrome odd-length; the distinct sentinels `^` and `$` stop expansion without bounds checks. `p[i]` will be the radius at `i`.
Every position of the transformed string.
Inside the rightmost palindrome, position `i` mirrors `2·center − i`, so its radius is at least the mirror's (but not past `right`, which we haven't verified).
Compare beyond what's known. Every successful comparison pushes the right edge further, so all expansions together are O(n).
Track the palindrome reaching furthest right.
A radius `r` in `t` is a palindrome of length `r` in `s`; centred there are `(r + 1) / 2` palindromes of `s` (lengths r, r − 2, …). Sum in 64 bits.

steps.text: Position 5: the mirror gives a head start of 0; expanding reaches radius 0.
Position 6: the mirror gives a head start of 0; expanding reaches radius 5.
Position 7: the mirror gives a head start of 0; expanding reaches radius 0.
Each radius r covers (r + 1) // 2 palindromes centred there. Sum: 9.

walk.title: Manacher: put # between letters so every palindrome has odd length, and reuse the mirror image of the current widest palindrome to start each expansion far out.

takeaways.md:
- **Manacher** gives every centre's palindrome radius in O(n), via mirror reuse.
- Separators unify odd and even palindromes; sentinels remove bounds checks.
- From radii you can count palindromes or find the longest one.
